restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The outer K>0 conjunct duplicates positivity already present in every branch.
An empty admissible set has ENNReal infimum ∞.
The tail condition literally uses Measure.real.
The moment branch has both Measurable and AEMeasurable requirements.
Real powers use Real.rpow for every real p≥1.
There is no centering or independence assumption.
The second conclusion unfolds the definition of LocalDef002.
ambiguities: No external name for LocalDef002 is supplied.
Constructor labels are inferred from branch bodies and corroborated by LocalDef015.
The absolute-MGF bound and its λ-range are literal; no alternate normalization is implied.
The proposition asks for one indexed condition, though the common finiteness criterion suggests equivalence among the four.

binders: μ is a measure on Ω.
Existentially, i indexes four conditions and K : ℝ.
hypotheses: No global measurability hypothesis is imposed on X; it occurs inside the indexed conditions.
conclusions: LocalDef002 μ X < ∞ iff some indexed condition LocalDef003 μ X i K holds for some K>0.
LocalDef002 μ X equals inf {t : ENNReal | LocalDef001 μ X t}.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X t means t is nonzero and finite and, at K=t.toReal, X is measurable and ∫exp(λ|X|)dμ≤exp(Kλ) with integrability for every 0≤λ≤1/K.
LocalDef002 is the ENNReal infimum of all LocalDef001-admissible scales.

The four LocalDef003 branches are: μ.real{|X|≥t}≤2exp(-t/K) for every t≥0; ∫|X|^p dμ≤(Kp)^p with integrability for every real p≥1; the absolute-MGF condition; or ∫exp(|X|/K)dμ≤2 with integrability. Each branch requires measurability and K>0.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, the ENNReal infimum of positive finite scales satisfying the stated local absolute-MGF bound is finite exactly when X satisfies, for some positive constant, at least one of four conditions: an exponential tail bound, real-moment growth, the absolute-MGF bound, or a one-point exponential-integrability bound. The statement also repeats the defining infimum identity.
